description: A presented pairing grant plus the current instant to a valid-or-refused decision with exactly one enumerated reason. A grant is single-use and expires, and its lifetime depends on how it reached the person redeeming it: 300 seconds for one shown at the target machine, 600 seconds for one delivered out of band to the account owner. Both boundaries are inclusive-accept. Where more than one reason holds the order is fixed: alreadyUsed, then expired, then noSuchGrant is decided by recognition before either. An already-redeemed grant reports that fact whether or not it has also expired, because the two situations mean different things to the person holding it.

cases.description: The ordinary at-machine case: an unredeemed grant shown on the target's own screen and typed in well within its lifetime. Possession of the machine is direct evidence of the authority being granted.
The ordinary out-of-band case: an unredeemed grant delivered to the owner's established address and redeemed well within its lifetime.

An at-machine grant presented at exactly 300 seconds is valid. Inclusive-accept by decision rather than by whichever comparison operator an implementation happens to use, which is why it is paired with the case one second past.
301 seconds, one second past the at-machine lifetime, and refused as expired. The other half of the boundary: without both, an implementation using the wrong comparison passes.
An out-of-band grant presented at exactly 600 seconds is valid. The longer wall-clock lifetime absorbs mail delivery latency, which is not under anyone's control and routinely exceeds a minute.
601 seconds, one second past the out-of-band lifetime, and refused as expired.

At 450 seconds an at-machine grant has already expired while an out-of-band one has not. This half pins the at-machine side; without the pair, an implementation using one lifetime for both would pass every other case in this file.

The same 450-second age, delivered out of band, is still valid. Identical instants and identical state, differing only by delivery path, with opposite outcomes — which is what proves the two lifetimes are actually distinct.

A grant redeemed once and presented again while still within its lifetime. Reported as alreadyUsed rather than expired, because the two indicate different situations to the user: one means try again, the other means this code is spent.

Both reasons hold: the grant was redeemed and it has since expired. alreadyUsed surfaces, pinning the precedence. Single use is what makes a grant observed in transit worthless after the fact, so that is the fact worth reporting.

A grant the target never issued. Reported as noSuchGrant rather than expired: a mistyped or invented code is not an expiry problem, and telling the user it expired sends them to wait for a new one they already have.

A grant the target never issued, presented at an age that would also be past its lifetime. noSuchGrant surfaces: recognition is settled before anything is computed from the grant's own claimed fields, which a target has no reason to trust for a grant it did not issue.
